Quick question as we dig into the pricing: we have an integration that streams a recorded telehealth session into the API in 3 pieces (pre-roll metadata, the transcript chunk, and a short follow-up prompt). From our contract review it’s unclear whether Redwood bills each request separately (which would hit minimums/rounding three times) or whether the platform aggregates tokens across the short conversation window and bills once.

Attached a tiny example (Helix_convo_examples.txt) — service_id HHL-911. If you bill per-request, our expected monthly spend goes up ~12% vs aggregated billing. Can you confirm how session/window aggregation works, and whether enterprise customers can opt into a different rounding policy?

John — nice write-up, thanks for the concrete example. Short answer: for hosted API requests we bill on a per-request token basis by default, but we apply a "conversation-window aggregation" behavior for sequences of requests that meet two conditions: they share the same conversation_id and arrive within a configured aggregation window.

Here are the important details so you can map it to your integration:

- Aggregation window: 45 seconds (from first related request) for the current hosted plan. Requests that arrive within that window and use the same model + conversation_id are grouped for billing aggregation.
- Aggregation scope: aggregation sums input + output tokens across grouped requests; system/prefix tokens that are re-used across messages are counted once per window when cache-Keying is enabled.
- Rounding/minimums: we bill at 1-token granularity after aggregation. There is a 12-token minimum per aggregated billing record to account for fixed per-RPC overhead for small bursts. So three tiny requests that together are 9 tokens would be billed at the 12-token minimum once if they fall inside the same window, instead of 12 tokens x3.
- Dedicated/private: Dedicated capacity customers can request a custom aggregation window and lower minimums in their contract — typical enterprise amendments reduce the minimum to 6 tokens or move to pure per-token billing (no minimum) with a small monthly commitment.

For Helix Health specifically, if your integration consistently sends the three pieces inside ~30s and you enable conversation_id propagation and our KV-prefix caching, you should see the three requests aggregated into a single billing record and avoid triple-minimum charges.

Cc'ing Karthik and Sean to confirm how this interacts with committed usage discounts and whether we can offer a temporary rounding concession while you onboard.

—Marissa

Thanks Marissa — a couple of practical notes from pricing/ops: 

1) For customers moving from per-request billing to aggregation we typically offer a one-quarter transitional concession to make the math simple: we can apply a "rounding-differential credit" equal to the difference between pre-aggregation billed tokens and post-aggregation billed tokens for the first 90 days (capped at $5k) while they finish integration and enable conversation_id propagation.
2) That concession requires us to track request IDs and conversation_ids (we use logs) — Neha, can we surface a short sample report in the HubSpot deal so Helix can see the delta?
3) For Dedicated deals: as Marissa noted, minimums are negotiable. If Helix is willing to commit to a 12-month reserved capacity we can remove the 12-token minimum and move to pure per-token billing with a mechanic to true-up monthly consumption.

John — if you send the traffic pattern for a typical week we’ll produce a billing delta estimate and add it to the M.A.P.

—Karthik

Susan — thanks, and happy to move quickly. Per your asks:

- Written confirmation: aggregation window = 45s for hosted API, aggregation requires same conversation_id + same model version, and post-aggregation billing uses 1-token granularity with a 12-token minimum per aggregated record. I’ve added that exact wording into the short SOW.
- Dedicated commitments to waive minimums: options we commonly offer are:
  * 12-month commit: remove minimums; 6-month ramp and monthly consumption true-up (typical for mid-market)
  * 24-month commit: remove minimums + 10% commitment discount on per-token unit price (typical for larger enterprises)
  * Pay-as-you-go Dedicated (very rare): minimums apply unless a $X/month platform fee is accepted.
